questions.stem: A medical student examines a cross-section of a kidney. She identifies three distinct regions. Which correctly lists these regions from outermost to innermost?

options.text: Medulla, cortex, renal pelvis
Cortex, medulla, renal pelvis
Renal pelvis, cortex, medulla
Cortex, renal pelvis, medulla

questions.explanation: From outside to inside, the kidney consists of the cortex (outer region where filtration occurs), the medulla (middle region containing loops of Henle and collecting ducts), and the renal pelvis (inner region where urine collects before entering the ureter).

questions.stem: A patient has a blockage in their ureter. Which problem would this most directly cause?

options.text: Blood cannot enter the kidney for filtration
Urine cannot drain from the kidney to the bladder, causing the kidney to swell
The kidney would stop producing urine entirely
Urea would not be produced by the liver

questions.explanation: The ureter carries urine from the renal pelvis to the bladder. If blocked, urine backs up into the kidney causing swelling (hydronephrosis) and potential kidney damage. The kidney continues producing urine but it has nowhere to drain.

questions.stem: The renal artery supplies blood to the kidney and the renal vein carries blood away. How would the composition of blood in the renal vein differ from that in the renal artery?

options.text: Renal vein blood has more urea and more glucose
Renal vein blood has less urea and less excess water
Renal vein blood has more oxygen and more urea
Renal vein blood is identical to renal artery blood

questions.explanation: As blood passes through the kidney, urea and excess water are filtered out and excreted as urine. Therefore, blood leaving via the renal vein contains less urea and less excess water than blood entering via the renal artery.

questions.stem: Each kidney contains approximately one million nephrons. Why is it important that there are so many functional units in each kidney?

options.text: To store large volumes of urine before it reaches the bladder
To provide a very large total surface area for efficient filtration and reabsorption of blood
To produce red blood cells for the circulatory system
To ensure that each nephron only needs to filter blood once per day

questions.explanation: Having approximately one million nephrons per kidney provides an enormous total surface area for filtration and reabsorption. This allows the kidneys to efficiently filter all the blood in the body (about 180 litres per day) and precisely control the composition of blood.

questions.stem: A surgeon needs to remove one of a patient's kidneys due to a tumour. The patient is told they can live a normal life with one kidney. Why is this possible?

options.text: The remaining kidney will grow a replacement kidney beside it
The liver takes over the filtering function of the missing kidney
One kidney has enough nephrons to filter blood adequately, and it can enlarge slightly to increase its capacity
The body stops producing waste products when a kidney is removed

questions.explanation: Each kidney has approximately one million nephrons — far more than the minimum needed for survival. The remaining kidney can compensate by enlarging (hypertrophy) and increasing its filtration rate, maintaining adequate excretion of waste products.
